name: Ichimoku Kinkō Hyō / 一目均衡表
explanation: Tenkan and Kijun are midpoints of rolling high/low ranges; Senkou A averages those lines, Senkou B uses a longer range; the cloud is drawn forward and Chikou backward.
caveat: Separate calculation time from display offset. A historical Chikou plot is not information available at that plotted date.

name: Heikin Ashi / 平均足
explanation: Synthetic close averages OHLC; synthetic open averages the previous synthetic open and close. This smooths candle appearance.
caveat: Synthetic candle prices are not executable broker quotes.

name: Renko / 練行足
explanation: Adds bricks when price traverses a selected box size; time between bricks is irregular.
caveat: OHLC reconstruction can conceal path ambiguity; ATR-sized historical bricks may change with settings.

name: Kagi / 鉤足
explanation: Alternates vertical legs after a reversal threshold; prior swing breaks change line state.
caveat: Requires ordered price paths; chart-derived fills must use actual prices.

name: Point & Figure
explanation: Uses X/O columns for box-sized advances and declines, reversing after a configured box count.
caveat: Intrabar high/low ordering affects columns.

name: Line Break
explanation: Prints a new line when price exceeds thresholds from the preceding lines; reversals use a configurable line count.
caveat: Irregular chart events are not fixed-time candles.

name: KDJ / 随机指标
explanation: Normalizes close within a recent high/low range to RSV, smooths into K and D, then forms J = 3K − 2D.
caveat: TongDaXin SMA is recursive smoothing, not an ordinary simple moving average; J can exceed 0–100.

name: BBI / 多空指标
explanation: Averages four simple moving averages to form a combined bull/bear baseline; periods differ across implementations.
caveat: MyTT defaults use 3/6/12/20; a different script may use 24 for the last period.

name: BIAS / 乖离率 / Kairi
explanation: Measures percentage displacement from a moving average: 100 × (price − MA)/MA.
caveat: Same concept appears under several names; it is not several independent signals.

name: PSY / 心理线
explanation: Reports the percentage of up-closing bars in a rolling period; often accompanied by a smoothed signal.
caveat: Counts bar direction, not investor survey sentiment.

name: BRAR / 人气意愿指标
explanation: AR compares high−open to open−low; BR compares movement relative to the previous close, aggregated over a window.
caveat: Exact clipping and zero-denominator conventions vary.

name: CR / 能量指标
explanation: Compares upward and downward movement around the previous bar midpoint; aggregates into a relative strength ratio.
caveat: Different platforms may use different reference prices.

name: VR / 成交量比率
explanation: Compares volume accumulated on up bars with down-bar volume, allocating unchanged bars according to its formula.
caveat: Needs meaningful volume. CFD tick-volume VR has different economic meaning from exchange-volume VR.

name: DFMA / DMA indicator
explanation: Subtracts a long moving average from a short one and smooths the difference.
caveat: The name DMA also means dynamic moving average elsewhere; resolve the formula before porting.

name: EXPMA
explanation: Plots exponential moving averages at multiple lengths to compare trend direction and crossings.
caveat: Usually an EMA presentation variant rather than a new mathematical family.

name: TAQ
explanation: Builds a highest-high/lowest-low channel and its midpoint over a chosen window.
caveat: Close relative to a current-bar channel is not the same as breakout above the previous channel.

name: KTN
explanation: MyTT combines an EMA of typical price with ATR-based envelopes; belongs to the Keltner family.
caveat: Match typical-price source and ATR smoothing when comparing outputs.

name: XSII / 薛斯通道 II
explanation: Combines a smoothed price centre with percentage envelopes and a dynamic channel construction.
caveat: Treat this implementation as a defined variant; the name alone does not uniquely specify every platform version.

name: Chanlun / 缠论 / CZSC
explanation: Builds inclusion-adjusted bars, fractals, strokes, segments and central zones; signal modules describe structural relationships.
caveat: A central zone or stroke can change while forming. Modules are not independent profitable indicators.

name: SMA
explanation: Arithmetic mean of the last N observations, with equal weights.
caveat: Lookback units are bars, not automatically days.

name: EMA
explanation: Recursively updates the average using α = 2/(N+1); recent observations receive more weight.
caveat: Seed choice and warm-up affect cross-library parity.

name: Wilder RMA / SMMA
explanation: Recursive smoothing with α approximately 1/N after an initial seed.
caveat: Chinese SMA(X,N,M) uses α=M/N and is not identical to SMA arithmetic averaging.

name: WMA / LWMA
explanation: Weights recent samples linearly more heavily than older samples.
caveat: Check weight orientation and initial valid index.

name: DEMA / TEMA
explanation: DEMA = 2E1 − E2; TEMA = 3E1 − 3E2 + E3, using successive EMAs.
caveat: Lag compensation can overshoot and react more strongly to noise.

name: Tillson T3
explanation: Combines successive EMA filters with coefficients controlled by a volume-factor parameter.
caveat: The volume-factor parameter is a smoothing coefficient, not an observed volume series.

name: Hull Moving Average
explanation: Combines WMA at full and half length, then smooths the compensated result over approximately √N.
caveat: Integer rounding rules can produce platform differences.

name: ALMA
explanation: Applies Gaussian weights with configurable offset and spread across the rolling price window.
caveat: Finta's ALMA entry is a placeholder; use an actual implementation from another source.

name: KAMA
explanation: Uses an efficiency ratio to adjust smoothing between fast and slow limits.
caveat: A trend-adaptive line still requires warm-up and a precisely defined seed.

name: VIDYA
explanation: Changes EMA weight using a momentum/variability measure such as absolute CMO.
caveat: Variants differ. Finta's named VIDYA method raises NotImplementedError.

name: FRAMA
explanation: Estimates fractal dimension from subwindow ranges and maps it into an adaptive smoothing coefficient.
caveat: Window parity and coefficient bounds matter.

name: MAMA / FAMA
explanation: Uses Hilbert-transform phase behaviour to adapt moving-average speed; FAMA follows MAMA more slowly.
caveat: Finta's MAMA is a placeholder; other implementations are present.

name: McGinley Dynamic
explanation: Updates a moving baseline with a denominator dependent on the price-to-baseline ratio.
caveat: Numerical handling near zero needs review.

name: ZLEMA
explanation: Adds a lag compensation term to price before exponential smoothing.
caveat: Zero lag in a name does not mean future price is known.

name: Jurik Moving Average / RSX variants
explanation: Public scripts implement smooth adaptive lines or RSI-like oscillators carrying Jurik-related names.
caveat: A public approximation is not proof of identity with proprietary Jurik software.

name: Ehlers Super Smoother
explanation: A recursive low-pass filter uses period-derived coefficients and previous filter states to attenuate high-frequency variation.
caveat: Initialization and coefficient conventions affect outputs.

name: Ehlers Ultimate Smoother
explanation: A low-lag smoothing construction combines high-pass/all-pass relationships to preserve lower-frequency components.
caveat: Primary publication and official PineCodersTASC page are linked; no independently audited local implementation claimed.

name: Ehlers Roofing Filter
explanation: Combines high-pass detrending with low-pass smoothing to retain a selected cycle band.
caveat: Filter period is not a forecast horizon.

name: Ehlers Cyber Cycle
explanation: Smooths and detrends price with recursive terms to isolate oscillatory components.
caveat: Turning points can change on the current open bar.

name: Laguerre Filter / Laguerre RSI
explanation: Uses a sequence of Laguerre states; directional state changes can be normalized into an RSI-like output.
caveat: Gamma governs the responsiveness and smoothness trade-off.

name: Fisher / Inverse Fisher
explanation: Transforms a bounded input to emphasize extremes; inverse Fisher compresses an oscillator into bounded outputs.
caveat: Clipping near ±1 is essential for finite Fisher values.

name: Hilbert dominant cycle / sine / phasor
explanation: Estimates phase and cycle properties using Hilbert-transform approximations.
caveat: Unstable initial periods and phase wrap require explicit handling.

name: Kalman Filter
explanation: Predicts a latent price state and uncertainty, then updates using an uncertainty-dependent gain when a new price arrives.
caveat: Q/R assumptions specify the model; a filter is causal, a backward smoother uses future observations.

name: Moving Median / Hampel Filter
explanation: Median filtering reduces sensitivity to isolated outliers; Hampel logic identifies extreme deviations around a local median.
caveat: A centred window is noncausal unless results are delayed.

name: Gaussian / Butterworth filters
explanation: Low-pass filtering suppresses rapid fluctuations using Gaussian weights or recursive Butterworth coefficients.
caveat: Different implementations can be trailing or centred.

name: RSI
explanation: Normalizes smoothed average gains versus losses into a 0–100 oscillator.
caveat: Overbought can persist in a trend; default seed conventions differ.

name: Stochastic
explanation: Locates close within the rolling high-low range; smooths %K into %D.
caveat: Specify fast/slow smoothing and zero-range handling.

name: Stochastic RSI
explanation: Applies the stochastic range normalization to RSI values rather than raw prices.
caveat: Two indicator layers increase sensitivity and warm-up requirements.

name: Stochastic Momentum Index
explanation: Double-smooths close displacement from the range midpoint and normalizes by a smoothed half-range.
caveat: Distinct from SMI Ergodic and ordinary stochastic.

name: Connors RSI
explanation: Averages price RSI, RSI of the signed streak length, and the percentile rank of a one-bar return.
caveat: Percent-rank conventions and tie handling vary.

name: QQE / QQE MOD
explanation: Smooths RSI and builds adaptive trailing bands from RSI changes; QQE MOD combines two QQE states.
caveat: ATR-like smoothing operates on RSI changes, not automatically on price ranges.

name: WaveTrend
explanation: EMA-centres price, normalizes displacement by smoothed absolute deviation, then smooths the normalized series and a signal line.
caveat: Multiple scripts use different smoothing and threshold settings.

name: MACD / PPO / APO
explanation: Compares fast and slow averages; MACD/APO show absolute differences, PPO divides by the slow average.
caveat: These are related transformations, not independent evidence votes.

name: ROC / Momentum
explanation: ROC reports percentage change from N bars ago; momentum usually reports the absolute difference.
caveat: Compare normalized rather than raw point thresholds across the four markets.

name: CCI
explanation: Divides typical-price displacement from its mean by a scaled mean absolute deviation.
caveat: The standard deviation is not the denominator of classical CCI.

name: CMO
explanation: Normalizes the difference between summed gains and losses by their total.
caveat: Smoothing differs from RSI despite shared input changes.

name: TSI / SMI Ergodic
explanation: Normalizes double-smoothed price changes by double-smoothed absolute changes; a signal EMA can be added.
caveat: Do not confuse True Strength Index with Trend Strength Index.

name: Schaff Trend Cycle
explanation: Combines MACD with stochastic-style cycle normalization and smoothing.
caveat: Variants differ in recursive smoothing and lookbacks.

name: Coppock / KST / Special K
explanation: Combines and smooths rates of change over several horizons to represent longer and shorter momentum cycles.
caveat: Closely related families should not be counted as independent confirmations.

name: Ultimate Oscillator
explanation: Aggregates buying pressure relative to true range over three windows with fixed relative weights.
caveat: Check preceding-close definition and zero denominators.

name: DeMarker
explanation: Compares positive high changes with positive low decreases and normalizes their moving totals.
caveat: A bounded oscillator still does not by itself define an executable strategy.

name: ADX / DMI
explanation: Derives +DI and −DI from directional movement relative to true range, then smooths their normalized difference into ADX.
caveat: ADX strength is separate from +DI/−DI direction.

name: Aroon
explanation: Scales bars-since-high and bars-since-low into Up/Down lines; their difference forms an oscillator.
caveat: Tie handling for repeated extremes affects values.

name: Vortex
explanation: Normalizes cross-bar high/low movement sums by total true range to produce VI+ and VI−.
caveat: Confirm rolling window and first-bar conventions.

name: Choppiness / VHF
explanation: CHOP compares accumulated range to total window excursion; VHF compares directional excursion to total price movement.
caveat: These measure path efficiency or consolidation, not a guaranteed future breakout.

name: Efficiency Ratio
explanation: Absolute net change divided by the sum of absolute step changes measures directional path efficiency.
caveat: A high value describes a past path; it does not prove continuation.

name: Trend Strength / CTI / RCI
explanation: Correlation-based measures compare prices or their ranks with time to quantify directional consistency.
caveat: Pearson price correlation and rank correlation are distinct definitions.

name: Hurst Exponent
explanation: Estimates scaling/persistence using a particular statistical procedure and lookback.
caveat: Short-sample estimates are noisy; estimator choice matters.

name: Entropy
explanation: Summarizes dispersion or uncertainty of a chosen probability representation of the series.
caveat: Results depend on how probabilities or bins are constructed; not all entropy indicators measure the same object.

name: Bollinger Bands / %B / Width
explanation: Plots a moving centre with standard-deviation envelopes; %B locates price and bandwidth measures spread of the bands.
caveat: Touching a band is a description, not automatic mean reversion.

name: Keltner / STARC
explanation: Uses ATR/range-based envelopes around a moving-average centre.
caveat: ATR and standard deviation bands respond differently to gaps.

name: Donchian / Price Channel
explanation: Upper/lower lines are rolling extremes with a midpoint centre.
caveat: A breakout rule normally compares against an already known previous channel.

name: Squeeze / TTM-style squeeze
explanation: Detects Bollinger bands inside Keltner channels; momentum is displayed separately, often with a regression histogram.
caveat: Squeeze does not specify the eventual direction; branded versions need not share identical code.

name: ATR / NATR / ADR
explanation: ATR smooths gap-aware true range; NATR normalizes by price; ADR averages daily high-low spans.
caveat: Range units must match each instrument; ATR and ADR are not interchangeable.

name: Historical / Realized Volatility
explanation: Aggregates squared returns or their standard deviation, with an explicit sampling interval and annualization factor.
caveat: Trading sessions and annualization conventions change comparisons.

name: Rogers-Satchell range volatility
explanation: Combines log high/open, high/close, low/open and low/close products into a range-based variance estimate.
caveat: Requires strictly positive prices; an issue for unadjusted historical oil series containing nonpositive quotes.

name: Ulcer Index / drawdown
explanation: Measures depth and persistence of percentage drawdowns from recent highs.
caveat: Measures downside path risk rather than symmetric return volatility.

name: Supertrend
explanation: Creates ATR-multiple bands and carries a selected band forward according to price breaks and previous state.
caveat: Open-bar flips can disappear before the bar closes.

name: Chandelier Exit
explanation: Places stops an ATR multiple away from rolling highs/lows, with stateful tightening rules.
caveat: Exact prior-stop crossing logic matters for porting.

name: Parabolic SAR
explanation: Updates stop-and-reverse points using an acceleration factor and trend extremes.
caveat: Initial trend seed and acceleration caps affect switches.

name: HalfTrend
explanation: Uses rolling extremes, smoothed prices and persistent trend state to build a stepped trend line and ATR channel.
caveat: A named port must be checked against the actual author implementation.

name: UT Bot
explanation: Uses an ATR-distance trailing stop and price/short-average crossings to generate alerts.
caveat: The original publication is linked; a chart alert does not define position sizing or fill rules.

name: Chande Kroll / NRTR
explanation: Combines directional extremes or trailing reversals with volatility/percentage distances.
caveat: Different trailing stop families can produce strongly correlated signals.

name: OBV / PVT / ADL
explanation: OBV signs total volume by close direction; PVT weights volume by percentage return; ADL weights by close location within range.
caveat: These are three distinct price-volume accumulation rules.

name: CMF / Chaikin Oscillator
explanation: CMF normalizes accumulated money-flow volume; Chaikin Oscillator compares short and long EMA values of ADL.
caveat: Both depend on the meaning and completeness of volume.

name: MFI / Force / Ease of Movement
explanation: MFI normalizes signed typical-price flow; Force multiplies price change by volume; EOM relates midpoint movement to volume and range.
caveat: Do not treat CFD tick counts as centralized exchange turnover.

name: Klinger / VFI / FVE
explanation: Alternative volume-pressure calculations use price direction, range or volatility thresholds before smoothing or accumulation.
caveat: Filter thresholds and scaling vary substantially.

name: VWAP / Anchored VWAP
explanation: Computes Σ(price×volume)/Σ(volume) from a session or event anchor.
caveat: A price-only approximation cannot reproduce the same quantity; anchors must be known at decision time.

name: VWMA / EVWMA
explanation: VWMA uses a fixed rolling weighted window; EVWMA uses an elastic volume-sensitive update.
caveat: Not equivalent to session VWAP.

name: RVOL / Volume at Time
explanation: Compares current volume with historical expected volume, optionally matched by clock time.
caveat: Match comparable sessions and daylight-saving transitions.

name: Volume Profile / POC / VAH / VAL
explanation: Distributes traded volume across price bins; POC is the largest bin and value area is constructed around volume concentration.
caveat: OHLCV-only reconstruction is an estimate; session and binning rules affect levels.

name: TPO / Market Profile
explanation: Counts price-level visits across fixed time blocks; builds a distribution of time participation rather than volume.
caveat: Time-at-price is different from actual volume-at-price.

name: Delta / Cumulative Delta
inputs: Aggressor-classified trades or an explicitly stated proxy
explanation: Delta sums buyer-initiated minus seller-initiated volume; CVD accumulates it over an anchor period.
caveat: TradingView intrabar direction estimates and true bid/ask aggressor data are not equivalent.

name: Footprint / Imbalance / Absorption
inputs: Bid/ask trades by price + ordered events
explanation: Displays buy/sell volume by price, tests imbalance ratios and relates aggressive flow to price response.
caveat: Cannot reconstruct true absorption or bid/ask footprint from four OHLC numbers.

name: DOM / Order-book imbalance
explanation: Compares displayed bid and ask depth, updates, cancellations and queue behaviour.
caveat: Displayed liquidity is not executed volume; spoofing and feed coverage affect interpretation.

name: Opening Range / Initial Balance
explanation: Records high/low of a predetermined opening window; monitors price relative to the completed range.
caveat: Do not use the final opening-range high before that opening window has ended.

name: Pivot Points / CPR / Camarilla
explanation: Calculates deterministic reference levels from the preceding session, with different formula families.
caveat: Session boundaries and method names must be explicit.

name: Fractals / Zigzag / Swing pivots
explanation: Identifies local extrema with right-side confirmation or reversal thresholds and connects significant swings.
caveat: Confirmed historical pivot location is earlier than the moment it became knowable.

name: BOS / CHoCH
explanation: Marks breaks of swing levels, distinguishing continuation and possible change in structural direction.
caveat: Definitions depend on pivot confirmation, close/wick rules and lag.

name: Order Blocks
explanation: Labels a preceding price area associated with a defined structural impulse and tracks mitigation.
caveat: Price-bar order blocks do not directly identify institutional inventory.

name: FVG / Inverse FVG
explanation: A three-bar gap condition marks nonoverlap between the first and third bars; inverse variants track later invalidation/reuse.
caveat: Some implementations attach the result to the middle bar before the third bar actually exists.

name: Liquidity Sweeps / EQH / EQL
explanation: Clusters similar highs/lows and detects excursions through a level followed by a specified rejection.
caveat: A sweep label is a rule-based price pattern, not proof of stop orders in the book.

name: Previous Day/Week High-Low
explanation: Projects already completed prior-session extremes as reference levels.
caveat: Broker days, New York sessions and exchange sessions produce different boundaries.

name: Fibonacci / Pitchfork / Regression channels
explanation: Projects ratios, median-line parallels or statistical trend channels from selected price anchors.
caveat: Automatically selected historical anchors may revise as later pivots arrive.

name: Harmonics: Gartley / Bat / Butterfly / Crab / Shark / Cypher
explanation: Classifies multi-leg structures by constrained retracement and extension ratios.
caveat: Ratio tolerances and pivot definitions are part of the method; a pattern name is not a full algorithm.

name: Elliott Wave
explanation: Labels nested impulse/correction structures subject to a chosen set of wave constraints.
caveat: Competing valid counts and relabelling make retrospective chart appearance unreliable as live evidence.

name: Wyckoff / VSA / Weis Wave
explanation: Examines price spread, volume, tests and wave accumulation to describe accumulation/distribution hypotheses.
caveat: Narrative labels must become deterministic rules before testing; volume quality matters.

name: Gann / square-of-nine / time cycles
explanation: Constructs geometric price/time levels from explicit scaling and anchor conventions.
caveat: A line angle changes with chart scaling; claims require a precise invariant definition.

name: Candlestick pattern families
explanation: Algorithms compare body, wick, gap and relative-size relationships across one or more bars.
caveat: Pattern outputs describe candle arrangements, not calibrated win probabilities; trend context may not be checked.

name: Nadaraya-Watson envelope / smoother
explanation: Uses kernel-weighted averages to estimate a smooth curve and optional residual bands.
caveat: A trailing endpoint estimate can be causal; a centred/repainting display uses future observations relative to older bars.

name: Lorentzian Classification / kNN
explanation: Uses a Lorentzian-style distance and approximate neighbour selection to classify future-direction labels from historical examples.
caveat: Training-label availability, neighbour chronology and in-sample selection must be checked in the actual code.

name: Adaptive ML Supertrend
explanation: Clusters historical volatility into regimes and uses a selected cluster representative in a Supertrend calculation.
caveat: Volatility clustering is not proof of price prediction; fitting must use only past observations.

name: COT Index / net positioning
explanation: Transforms participant net positions, changes or historical min-max ranks into contextual series.
caveat: Weekly observation date is not public release time; never backfill Tuesday knowledge into a live decision before publication.

name: Open Interest / price-OI regimes
explanation: Measures outstanding contracts and combines OI changes with price changes to describe participation.
caveat: Not a spot CFD field; contract rolls and aggregation affect the series.

name: Options IV / skew / term structure / gamma
explanation: Summarizes option-implied uncertainty and exposure across strikes and expiries.
caveat: Dealer gamma sign and ownership are often estimated rather than directly observed.

name: Intermarket ratios / rolling correlation / beta
explanation: Compares markets using ratios, covariances, rolling regressions or residuals.
caveat: Availability timestamps and different trading hours matter; relationships may change sign.

name: Seasonality / session statistics
explanation: Groups past observations by month, weekday or exchange-session clock to describe recurring distributions.
caveat: Avoid full-sample averages that leak the evaluation period into its own reference.

name: EIA inventories / crude time spreads
inputs: EIA releases + separately quoted futures maturities
explanation: Inventory changes describe physical balances; near/far futures spreads describe the term structure.
caveat: Release timestamp, revisions and contract identity are required; a CFD candle alone cannot supply these data.

name: Gold real-yield / dollar / GVZ context
inputs: FRED real yields + dollar reference + options volatility
explanation: Adds separate macro/volatility series alongside gold prices for analysis.
caveat: These are contextual data inputs, not a guaranteed negative or positive relationship with gold.

name: Nasdaq breadth / VXN / relative strength
explanation: Measures participation across constituent stocks, implied volatility or relative performance versus a reference index.
caveat: Use historical constituents and weights to avoid survivorship bias; QQQ is a reference feed in this project.

name: DAX session / breadth / volatility context
inputs: Eurex/Xetra sessions + constituents + optional volatility data
explanation: Aligns futures, cash-index trading and constituent participation to a documented exchange session.
caveat: DAX cash, FDAX futures and a broker CFD are distinct series and can have different prices/hours.
